linkedin:
A breeder who registers a cultivar with most genetics databases is handing over their life's work to whoever runs the database. StrainChain doesn't breed, sell, license or take an option on any genetics it records — that commitment sits on the passport page itself, not only in a policy document.

The dossier is built to be the breeder's defensive record, not our catalogue: something they control and can export, not an entry in someone else's collection. Every parent/child lineage edge is tagged as confirmed in writing, inferred, claimed, or no evidence at all — an inferred cross is never rendered as a confirmed one, because a defensive record that overstates its own evidence isn't defensible.

The chemistry side gets the same treatment. Cannabis certificates of analysis print a "total THCV" or "total THC" as a decarboxylation-weighted sum sitting on top of raw values; StrainChain recomputes that total from the raw panel at render time instead of trusting the certificate's own printed line, and shows it plainly if the two disagree.

Each cultivar page also carries a checksum computed from the certificates and lineage shown, reproducible from the published bytes — we're upfront that on its own it says what the record contains, not when it existed; it isn't a timestamp or a priority claim, just something a breeder (or anyone else) can recompute and check against.

https://strainchain.io/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=genetics-record-fingerprint&utm_content=b

reddit.title: Building a cannabis genetics registry that structurally can't become a breeding competitor to the people who use it
reddit.body:
I work on StrainChain, a cannabis-provenance/genetics tool. The design question behind this build: genetics databases in this industry have a trust problem once they get big enough to be useful, because the same aggregated data that helps a breeder document their cultivar is also exactly what a breeding program would want.

Our answer was to make the commitment structural rather than a policy line: StrainChain doesn't breed, sell, license or option any genetics it records, and that commitment is stated on the passport page itself. The dossier is framed as the breeder's own defensive record — something they can export and take with them — not an entry in a catalogue we control.

The evidence handling follows the same principle. Lineage between cultivars (parent/child crosses) is tagged confirmed in writing, inferred, claimed, or no evidence, and an inferred cross is never shown as confirmed. Cannabis certificates of analysis also report a computed "total THCV"/"total THC" on top of raw values; we recompute that total from the raw panel at render time and surface it if it disagrees with what the certificate printed, rather than just repeating the certificate's number.

Each page also carries a checksum over what's shown, reproducible from the published bytes — though we say plainly it's not a timestamp or a claim of who had a cross first.

For people who've registered genetics anywhere before: does a stated non-breeding commitment actually change whether you'd trust a registry with your cultivar, or is that promise something everyone claims until they don't?

https://strainchain.io/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=genetics-record-fingerprint&utm_content=b

Disclosure: I work on this project.
